implementation_notes: The standard library ships the fallible-value combinators: `Result` has `map`/`flatMap`/`mapError`/`flatMapError`, `Optional` has `map`/`flatMap`, `try?` converts a thrown error into an optional, and `Sequence`/`Collection` provide `map`/`filter`/`reduce`. Chains of these replace exception-driven class hierarchies and explicit `do`/`catch` ladders. The classic structure is still justified when the DSL crosses module boundaries: Swift has no higher-kinded types, so a generic combinator abstraction must be written per concrete type or hidden behind protocols with associated types, which cannot be used as values.
pitfalls: `Result` needs a concrete `Failure: Error`, so joining results with different error types requires `mapError` at every junction.
`try?` erases the error value: using it inside a combinator chain discards exactly the diagnostic information the DSL was built to carry.
No higher-kinded types: a generic 'any wrapper' combinator has to be re-implemented per type, and protocol-based abstractions cannot be stored or passed as values.

variants.name: Combine: Publisher operator chains
variants.idiom_name: Combine operators (map, flatMap, merge, zip, catch, retry) over Publisher
variants.implementation_notes: Combine realises the pattern for event streams: `Publisher` values compose with operators - `map`, `flatMap(maxPublishers:)`, `merge`, `combineLatest`, `zip`, `replaceError`, `retry` - and a chain is a declarative description assembled before a subscriber (`sink`/`assign`) drives it. Choose it when the domain is asynchronous events (UI, networking) on Apple platforms; choose the standard library variant for plain value pipelines, because Combine is platform-bound and each publisher fixes its own `Failure` type.
pitfalls: Publishers are lazy and cold: nothing runs until a subscriber attaches, and the returned `AnyCancellable` must be retained or the subscription is cancelled immediately.
`flatMap`/`merge` require matching `Failure` types, so error propagation forces explicit `mapError`/`catch` steps - a frequent source of compile-error walls.
`Publishers.FlatMap` can subscribe to an unbounded number of upstream publishers: without `maxPublishers`, a burst of events launches a storm of requests.
